title: Affine-base restriction maps for projective spectra of a graded algebra sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ a graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra whose homogeneous components are quasi-coherent, as in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For every affine open $U\subseteq X$ put $P_U=\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(U,\mathcal A))$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], with $p_U:P_U\to U$ induced by $\mathcal O_X(U)\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)_0$. For affine opens $V\subseteq U$, the graded restriction homomorphism induces a canonical morphism $r^U_V:P_V\to P_U$ over $U$. This morphism identifies $P_V$ with the open subscheme $p_U^{-1}(V)$ over $V$. It is the identity when $V=U$ and satisfies $r^U_W=r^U_V\circ r^V_W$ whenever $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ are affine opens.

proof.text: The underlying module of $\mathcal A$ is the sheaf coproduct of the quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal A_n$ by [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure] to the small index set $\mathbb N$: the underlying module is quasi-coherent. Thus the affine algebra inclusion theorem is applicable to $\mathcal A$ itself, without finite generation and without assuming $\mathcal A_0=\mathcal O_X$. For an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}Q$, set $M_n=\Gamma(T,\mathcal A_n)$. Clauses (3) and (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identify the sheaf coproduct on $T$ with $\widetilde{\bigoplus_n M_n}$, compatibly with the summand inclusions. Clause (2) then identifies $\Gamma(T,\mathcal A)=\bigoplus_n M_n$. Thus the sections used below have the asserted grading, not merely a family of homogeneous submodules.

proof.text: Fix affine opens $V\subseteq U$. Put $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $S=\mathcal O_X(V)$, $C=\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)$ and $D=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$. Clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-affine-inclusion] gives the ring isomorphism $C\otimes_R S\to D$, $a\otimes s\mapsto s\,a|_V$. Swap the tensor factors to write it as $\beta:S\otimes_R C\to D$, $s\otimes a\mapsto s\,a|_V$. This swap respects multiplication since both rings are commutative. The tensor module has the direct-sum decomposition $S\otimes_R C=\bigoplus_n(S\otimes_R C_n)$: maps from either side to any $S$-module are exactly families of $R$-balanced bilinear maps $S\times C_n$ into that module, so the balanced-tensor and direct-sum universal properties give inverse comparisons. Restriction preserves every homogeneous component by [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], and $S$ acts in degree zero, so $\beta$ is graded. Its inverse preserves degree as well: decompose a preimage into homogeneous components and use injectivity to kill every component of a different degree. The induced map $a\mapsto\beta(1\otimes a)$ is precisely restriction $C\to D$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] with $(A,B)=(C,D)$ and the graded isomorphism $\beta$ from Step 2. It gives a morphism $r^U_V:P_V\to P_U$ on all of $P_V$, with inverse-image charts $D_+(f|_V)$ and ring maps $a/f^m\mapsto(a|_V)/(f|_V)^m$. Its cartesian square has bottom map $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to S)$, which is the affine open inclusion $V\hookrightarrow U$ under the affine identifications in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-affine-inclusion], with spectrum functoriality as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The vertical maps are exactly $p_U,p_V$, since their degree-zero maps are the algebra units. Hence $p_U\circ r^U_V$ is $p_V$ followed by this inclusion.

The open subscheme $p_U^{-1}(V)$ represents the fibre product $P_U\times_U V$: a map into it is exactly a map into $P_U$ whose composite into $U$ factors through the open subscheme $V$, and that factorization is unique. Indeed, a map $a:T\to P_U$ whose base map factors through $V$ has image in $p_U^{-1}(V)$. Restrict its continuous map to that open and its structure-sheaf map to $\mathcal O_{P_U}|_{p_U^{-1}(V)}$; the maps on stalks are unchanged and hence remain local. This gives the required scheme morphism, and composing with the open inclusion recovers $a$. Both the continuous map and the sheaf map are forced by this equality. This uses the description of an open subscheme in [def-weil-open-immersion]. By the uniqueness clause of [def-pc-fibre-product], the cartesian square in Step 3 identifies $P_V$ with $p_U^{-1}(V)$ over $V$, and its first projection is $r^U_V$.

proof.text:
For $V=U$, the chart maps of [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] send every fraction $a/f^m$ to itself. They are identity ring maps, so their spectrum maps are identities by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the chart cover gives $r^U_U=\mathrm{id}$. For affine $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$, write $f_V=f|_V$ and $f_W=f|_W$. The inverse image of $D_+(f)$ under either proposed composite is $D_+(f_W)$, and on its coordinate rings the composite is
$$a/f^m\longmapsto(a|_V)/f_V^m\longmapsto((a|_V)|_W)/f_W^m=(a|_W)/f_W^m.$$
The last equality is the restriction axiom of the sheaf algebra [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. This is the chart map of $r^U_W$. Fractions represent all elements of these chart rings [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], so the ring maps agree; their spectrum maps agree by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The opens $D_+(f_W)$ cover $P_W$ by the scalar-extension node, hence [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], specifically its uniqueness clause, makes equality of these restrictions equality of the scheme morphisms. Thus $r^U_W=r^U_V\circ r^V_W$.
